findings.title: Concurrent-delete NPE remains in filtered and paged sub-group methods
findings.body: The three getSubGroupsStream overloads at lines 254-269 still dereference modelSupplier.get() without a null check. That supplier ultimately calls getGroupById, which can return null when another transaction deletes the group after this cached adapter was created. A concurrent delete therefore still causes a NullPointerException for filtered or paged sub-group access, even though the same race was fixed for getSubGroupsCount. These overloads should handle a null delegate consistently, for example by returning an empty stream.

findings.title: getSubGroupsCount now violates its non-null count contract
findings.body: For an existing group, the delegate's count query returns a non-null Long, but this change returns null when the group was concurrently deleted. That null is propagated by GroupUtils.populateSubGroupCount into GroupRepresentation.subGroupCount, changing the API value from a number to null and risking a later, harder-to-diagnose NullPointerException in consumers that unbox the count. Returning 0L for a deleted group would avoid the original NPE while preserving the method's non-null contract.

findings.title: Reader thread is neither joined nor reliably stopped before the assertion
findings.body: The reader thread started at line 139 is never joined. The main thread sets deletedAll at line 155 and asserts at line 157 that no exceptions were captured, but an in-flight groups() call can still fail and add an exception after that assertion, producing a false pass. Conversely, if a group removal throws before line 155, deletedAll is never set and the non-daemon reader keeps issuing requests after the test, potentially interfering with later tests. The flag should be set in a finally block, the thread should be retained and joined with a timeout before asserting, and coordination should guarantee that polling actually overlapped the deletions.
